column3: The exact hearing-knowing formula joins mercy to informed divine response, but supplies no local idol contrast.
Refuge in the all-hearing, all-knowing God supports reliance under hostile prompting.
Sets receptive hearing of God's word against ignorance, directly opposing unhearing false carriers.
The exact formula frames divine response to a hidden plot, without the focus's idol setting.
The immediate warning against another god establishes the false-worship contrast completed by 26:220.
Repeats the divine attributes in a provision setting without developing hearing or false mediation.
Divine knowledge supports authoritative assurance, but hearing and the local contrast are absent.
The immediate command to rely on the Mighty, Merciful receives its perceptive ground in 26:220.
Distinguishes the learned, but does not clarify divine hearing or unhearing worship.
Reliance is expressly grounded in the same all-hearing, all-knowing declaration.
Truth's defeat of fabricated work gives a secondary contrast to false religious agency.
God's knowledge of hostile speech makes the same formula a direct ground for steadiness.
Forgiveness and affection add no hearing, knowledge, or worship-capacity relation.

God's knowledge of concealed and public speech explains why hostile words need not unsettle the messenger.

Divine sight of the messenger when he stands is the immediate observation frame for 26:220.
Revelation sent with divine knowledge supports a true divine source over false carriers.
A warning continuous with earlier warners echoes the local commission to warn, but indirectly.
The magicians' prostration after truth becomes clear resonates with the focus's observed prostration.
Lack of knowledge of revealed limits is only a distant contrast with divine knowledge.
God's knowledge of every utterance and the exact formula reinforce comprehensive divine perception.
The immediate instruction to disavow disobedient acts lies within the same divinely observed mission sequence.
The formula connects present conduct to meeting God but adds no specific hearing or idol relation.
The all-aware judge is broadly related, yet the hearing pair and local contrast are missing.
Night recitation and prostration resonate with the focus's movement among prostrators.
Deferring uncertain knowledge to God is not a focused instance of divine hearing.
The greatness of the warning supplies no hearing or knowledge connection.
The envoys' fear is answered by the nearby assurance of divine hearing and sight.
Hearing a revealed book and recognizing its guidance models receptive hearing opposite to false carriers.
God alone judges while those invoked besides Him cannot; His perception directly sharpens the idol contrast.
God's assurance that He hears and sees the envoys closely parallels the focus's protective perception.
Limited human knowledge versus divine knowledge is broad and lacks a hearing or worship route.
The Creator's intimate knowledge supplies a clear basis for comprehensive divine awareness.
Standing, sitting, and prostration extend the embodied worship pattern seen by God in the focus context.
The statement of divine favor and knowledge offers no distinct hearing relation.
The highest horizon has no material connection to the focus reading.
Nighttime prostration and standing resonate with the focus's observed worshipful movement.
Future knowledge is too general to develop the hearing-knowing declaration.
The powerless objects invoked besides God are directly opposed to the all-hearing, all-knowing God.
Truthful recitation supports revelation generally but does not specify hearing or false mediation.
Personal recognition of what one brought is only a broad accountability relation.
The exact formula accompanies a prayer for acceptance, without the focus's contrast or mission setting.
Active worship and hastening to good continue the prostration-centered resonance.
Comprehensive knowledge secures prior clarification, but hearing is not developed.
The formula accompanies divine sufficiency in a dispute, with no focused perceptive relation.
The blindness-sight contrast is only indirectly related to perceptive divine oversight.
Knowledge of the unseen and sight of deeds supports the focus's continuous divine observation.
The all-hearing, all-seeing declaration accompanies a divinely guided journey, echoing protective perception.
Future knowing is a general warning rather than a hearing-knowing connection.
The formula in a vow of dedication adds no local worship-capacity contrast.
Deferred knowledge after heedlessness remains too general for the focus reading.
Seeking refuge in the all-hearing, all-seeing God parallels reliance under hostile opposition.
The repeated future knowledge remains a general warning.
Divine knowledge and wisdom support patience but omit hearing and the focus's false-worship contrast.
Hearing creation's signs is a receptive-hearing echo, but the connection is indirect.
The formula in a divorce ruling is a generic repetition without a related setting.
Human loss of knowledge in old age does not clarify divine hearing and knowledge.
Prostration and divine wise knowledge provide a secondary resonance with observed worshipful movement.
The direct question whether idols hear those who call them is the focus's central contrary pole.
Repentance and mercy add no hearing, knowledge, or worship-capacity relation.
The announcement of a knowing boy does not develop the focus reading.
The exact refuge formula repeats the reliance-under-perception pattern of 41:36.
The command to hear follows testimony procedure, but does not identify divine hearing or false worship.
The generic hearing-knowing formula adds no distinct context.
The same-surah assurance that God is listening directly grounds prophetic action under divine perception.
The formula accompanies a battle command and adds no focused hearing relation.
Hearing God's word, understanding it, then knowingly distorting it exposes a false human carrier.
Changing a heard directive makes the listener accountable before the all-hearing, all-knowing God.
Pharaoh's demand that his circle listen illustrates an attempted human control of hearing within the same surah.
The calf episode supplies an idolatry counterpoint, though it does not explicitly address hearing.
God's universal knowledge preserved in a record supports the focus's comprehensive knowing.
The formula follows troop placement without developing divine hearing or knowledge.
Freedom from vain speech is only a remote sound-related parallel.
The formula in a hostile spending context is a generic repetition.
Hearing the signs in the ordered night and day pattern models receptive recognition.

Divine testimony with the knowledgeable establishes a true, just source of religious knowledge.
The public call to hear a confession of faith presents hearing as a demanded response.
The formula is attached to inner change and remains a generic divine-attribute repetition.
The decisive-word statement has no material hearing or knowledge relation.
Knowing one's prior and deferred deeds supplies an accountability horizon for divine comprehensive knowledge.
The Qur'an's nobility alone does not clarify the focus declaration.
Recognition of revelation by prior learned authorities supports authentic transmission over false carriers.
Expectation of separation adds no relevant hearing or knowledge connection.
Seeking interpretive knowledge for the people is a distant knowledge-transfer parallel.
All-encompassing knowledge accompanies provision but lacks the hearing and worship contrast.
Human hearing, sight, and hearts are given for responsive gratitude, contrasting failed reception.
The revealer who knows secrets establishes the Qur'an's true source against false hidden carriers.
Hearing recited signs yet persistently refusing them sharply distinguishes mere audition from receptive hearing.
The denial that devils brought down the Qur'an directly protects revelation from false carriers.
It states that demonic delivery neither befits nor is possible for them, sharpening the source contrast.
Their exclusion from hearing directly opposes the all-hearing God named in 26:220.
The immediate question about those on whom devils descend introduces the false-carrier contrast.
The descent upon every sinful liar identifies the opposed kind of purported religious carrier.
They relay what they hear while most lie, making false transmission the direct counterpoint to divine knowledge.
The same-sura idol scene introduces the objects whose inability to hear is tested in 26:72.
Idols' inability to benefit or harm further exposes the inadequacy of beings invoked beside God.
Those invoked besides God are challenged to answer their callers, directly testing their claimed agency.
Invoked beings cannot aid their callers or themselves, reinforcing the focus's anti-idol contrast.
Calling such beings to guidance produces no response, a direct parallel to the unhearing-idol polemic.
It forbids invoking what neither benefits nor harms apart from God, matching the local idol argument.
Those called besides God do not answer, contrasting their impotence with God's complete perception.
The beings invoked besides God create nothing and are themselves created, undermining false divine carriers.
They are lifeless and unaware, directly opposing the living, all-knowing God.
Claimed beings besides God cannot remove or transfer harm, extending the critique of rival invocation.
It rejects worship of what can neither benefit nor harm, a close formulation of the idol critique.
Those invoked besides God cannot create even a fly, demonstrating their total incapacity.
False gods cannot create, harm, benefit, cause death, give life, or raise, directly contrasting divine sufficiency.
Claimed partners possess nothing and have no share or supporting power in creation.
The false invokees possess no dominion, exposing the lack of authority behind rival calls.
They do not hear callers and, even if they heard, could not answer; this is the closest direct parallel.
The admission that God creates all exposes the inconsistency of invoking powerless rivals.
No one is further astray than one who invokes beings that will not answer and are unaware of the call.
It forbids calling anyone alongside God, directly repeating the prohibition that frames 26:220.
